exercises.title: University words (Ex. 2)
exercises.instruction: Read the signs displayed in a local university. Match the words in bold with the definitions 1–10.

items.left: a formal talk given to a group of people in order to teach them about a subject
items.explanation: lecture — bài giảng trước đông người.

items.left: to become or make someone become an official member of a course, college or group
items.explanation: enrol — đăng ký nhập học/ghi danh vào khoá học.

items.left: to provide money for an event, activity or organisation
items.explanation: fund — cấp vốn, tài trợ.

items.left: a piece of work or job that you are given to do
items.explanation: assignment — bài tập được giao.

items.left: the land and buildings belonging to a college or university
items.explanation: campus — khuôn viên trường đại học.

items.left: a particular department at a college or university, or the teachers in that department
items.explanation: faculty — khoa (và giảng viên của khoa).

items.left: a higher university qualification that usually takes one or two more years of study after your first degree
items.explanation: Master's degree — bằng thạc sĩ (học thêm 1–2 năm sau cử nhân).

items.left: a student who is studying for their first university degree
items.explanation: undergraduate — sinh viên đại học (chưa có bằng đầu tiên).

items.left: a university degree that is given after a course of study that usually takes three or four years
items.explanation: Bachelor's degree — bằng cử nhân (3–4 năm).

items.left: a student who has one degree and is now studying at a university for a more advanced degree
items.explanation: postgraduate — học viên sau đại học (đã có một bằng).

exercises.title: Study the flow-chart (Ex. 3)
exercises.instruction: Look at the flow-chart "Applying to study at university in Australia (for international students)", ignoring the gaps for the moment. Answer the questions. (1: Once you have chosen, you can apply ___ to the university for a place. 2: Once you have confirmation of ___ 3: and adequate ___ for the first year… 4: especially for ___ students.)

items.prompt: What does the title suggest the chart is about?

options.text: how to apply to an Australian university as an international student
how to find a job in Australia

items.explanation: Tiêu đề 'Applying to study at university in Australia (for international students)' → cách nộp hồ sơ vào đại học Úc cho sinh viên quốc tế.

items.prompt: What type of word is missing in gap 1 (apply ___ to the university)?
items.explanation: Bổ nghĩa cho động từ apply → trạng từ.

items.prompt: What type of word is missing in gap 2 (confirmation of ___)?
items.explanation: Sau giới từ of → danh từ.

items.prompt: What type of word is missing in gap 3 (adequate ___)?
items.explanation: Sau tính từ adequate → danh từ.

items.prompt: What type of word is missing in gap 4 (for ___ students)?
items.explanation: Trước danh từ students → tính từ.

exercises.title: Complete the flow-chart (Ex. 4)
exercises.instruction: Read the short text and then complete the flow-chart using ONE WORD ONLY from the text.

stimulus.text:
Studying abroad

Studying abroad as an international student can be an enriching experience. If you have a good level of English, you will face the difficult decision of deciding which university you would like to apply to. Once you have chosen, you can contact the university directly in order to apply.

In order to successfully obtain a place at university, you will need to get a visa to study at the university of your choice. In order to obtain a visa, you will need proof of admission to the college. You will also need to show that you have enough funds for the first year of study. After you have done this, you can apply for a visa. Once you have received a visa, you can start to look for flights and also try to find somewhere to live. This is something that you don't need to worry about, as each university has an accommodation team to help you. Furthermore, preferential treatment is given for new students from abroad.
stimulus.caption: Studying abroad (p. 129)

items.prompt: Step 1 – Choose a university and enrol: Once you have chosen, you can apply ____ to the university for a place.
items.explanation: "you can contact the university **directly** in order to apply".

items.prompt: Step 2 – Apply for a student visa: Once you have confirmation of ____ and adequate ____ for the first year, you can apply for your visa.
items.explanation: "you will need proof of **admission**… enough **funds** for the first year".

items.prompt: Step 3 – Book your flight and accommodation: each university has an accommodation team that can help you find a place, especially for ____ students.
items.explanation: "preferential treatment is given for **new** students from abroad".

exercises.title: University signs (Ex. 11)
exercises.instruction: Study these university signs. Which sentence in each pair is most likely to be correct and why?

items.prompt: 1a YOU MUST NOT EAT IN CLASSROOMS. / 1b YOU DON'T HAVE TO EAT IN CLASSROOMS.

options.text: 1a — it expresses a rule, something which is not allowed

items.explanation: Biển báo nêu quy định cấm → must not; 'don't have to' (không bắt buộc) không hợp lý.

items.prompt: 2a YOU DON'T HAVE TO CHEAT IN THE EXAM. / 2b YOU MUST NOT CHEAT IN THE EXAM.

options.text: 2b — it expresses a rule, something which is not allowed

items.explanation: Gian lận bị cấm → must not cheat; 'don't have to cheat' vô lý.

items.prompt: 3a You don't have to return your library book to the reception desk – you can also use the boxes provided. / 3b You must not return your library book to the reception desk – you can also use the boxes provided.

options.text: 3a — it expresses an idea which is optional
3b — returning books to reception is not allowed

items.explanation: "you can also use the boxes" → có lựa chọn → don't have to.

exercises.title: How were the words explained? (Ex. 16–17)
exercises.instruction: How were these words explained in the texts: by footnote, an explanation in the text, or an explanation given by the surrounding context?

stimulus.text:
How the modern computer works

The mouse and keyboard are input units: ways of getting information into your computer. Most computers store all this information on a hard drive (a huge magnetic memory). However, smaller computer-based devices like digital cameras and mobile phones use other kinds of storage, such as flash memory cards.

The computer's processor, also known as the central processing unit, is a microchip* buried deep inside. As it is used it becomes incredibly hot and a fan prevents the computer from overheating.

Many computers now have LCD screens, capable of displaying high-resolution graphics, such as very clear and detailed photographs. Many computers also have loudspeakers and can be connected to a printer.

*microchip – a very small part of a computer or machine that does calculations or stores information
stimulus.caption: How the modern computer works (p. 133)

"a piece of cloth with ink on it called the ribbon".
carriage return lever — đoán nghĩa nhờ ngữ cảnh xung quanh.
"a hard drive (a huge magnetic memory)".
"other kinds of storage, such as flash memory cards".
"such as very clear and detailed photographs".
microchip được giải thích bằng footnote.

exercises.title: Advice or obligation? (Ex. 8)
exercises.instruction: Look at phrases a–c taken from the text: a I have to attend three lectures a week · b you must have a great deal of self-discipline · c you should choose something you will enjoy.

items.prompt: Which of these statements expresses advice?
items.explanation: should = lời khuyên → câu c.

items.prompt: Which two of these statements express an obligation?
items.explanation: have to và must = nghĩa vụ → câu a và b.

items.prompt: Which of these statements expresses a strong obligation?
items.explanation: must = nghĩa vụ mạnh (người nói tự thấy bắt buộc) → câu b.

items.prompt: What is the past tense of "I have to attend"?
items.explanation: Quá khứ của have to là had to.

items.prompt: What is the past tense of "you should choose something you will enjoy"?

options.text: You should have chosen something you would enjoy.
You should chose something you would enjoy.

items.explanation: should + choose → should have + V3 (should have chosen); will → would.

exercises.title: Strength of obligation (Ex. 10)
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences to show strength of obligation. More than one answer is possible.

items.prompt: I ____ study harder. (strong obligation)
items.explanation: Nghĩa vụ mạnh → must / have to.

items.prompt: I ____ go to school today. (no obligation)
items.explanation: Không bắt buộc → don't have to / needn't.

items.prompt: You ____ revise for your exams this weekend. (advice)
items.explanation: Lời khuyên → should / ought to.

items.prompt: You ____ be late for lessons. (strong negative obligation)
items.explanation: Cấm (nghĩa vụ phủ định mạnh) → mustn't.

exercises.title: Which stage of education? (Ex. 1)
exercises.instruction: Which type of education is each of these about?

items.text: Children usually start in an early class called "Reception".
items.explanation: Reception là lớp đầu tiên của tiểu học ở Anh → mầm non / tiểu học.

items.text: Children learn to read and write in infant school.
items.explanation: Infant school (lớp nhỏ của tiểu học) dạy đọc, viết → tiểu học.

items.text: Students go to different classrooms for different subjects.
items.explanation: Đổi phòng theo môn học → trung học.

items.text: Students prepare for A levels for two years.
items.explanation: A levels học 2 năm ở sixth form → trung học / dự bị đại học.

items.text: A vocational course prepares students for work in a profession.
items.explanation: Vocational course (học nghề) → giáo dục bậc cao/thường xuyên (further education).

items.text: Students live away from home for the first time.
items.explanation: Lần đầu sống xa nhà → đại học (higher education).
Khoá học tối và cuối tuần giá rẻ → giáo dục cho người lớn (adult education).
